newsitem.title: USA: Dentist's wife guilty in hired shoplifter case.
newsitem.headline: Dentist's wife guilty in hired shoplifter case.

text.p: A jury Thursday found a dentist's wife guilty of receiving stolen goods from a thief who prosecutors alleged was hired to steal luxury items specifically ordered by the well-to-do family of four.
Judy Dick, 56, was found guilty by the Ramsey County Court jury of aiding and abetting receipt of stolen property, a felony, but was acquitted on a charge of conspiracy to obtain stolen goods.
Her husband Gerald Dick, 59, and his daughter Stacy Zehren, a 34-year-old Chicago attorney, were found innocent on both counts by the jury, which deliberated a day after a week-long trial.
As a first-time offender, Judy Dick would not serve time in prison but could be fined $10,000.

The much-publicised case revolved around convicted shoplifter Gregory Thomas, who claimed he had stolen items specifically requested by the Dick family for years, an allegation the jury appeared to reject in its verdict.

During the trial, Gerald Dick testified that he was unaware of the scheme, but had wondered why his wife had asked him for his dental blowtorch. Prosecutors contended the blowtorch was used to burn off security tags on stolen clothing.

Earlier during the trial, Judge Salvador Rosas dismissed charges against the couple's son James Dick, 33, a former part-time player on the Minnesota Vikings football team, ruling that police misstated the evidence to his lawyer.

The prosecution's case was marred by police errors and a disputed tape-recording. Thomas and a Dayton's Department Store security guard acting undercover sold the Dick family $7,000 worth of supposedly stolen Armani suits and Baccarat Crystal for less than $1,000.
The Dick's lawyers argued their clients were entrapped.
